chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'No servant gives good charity in this world except that God betters the succession over his children after him.'
And he said: 'Good charity pays off debts and leaves behind blessing.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Sadaqa — voluntary charitable giving, broader than zakat; includes any act of giving for God's sake
key_terms.الْبَرَكَة: Baraka — divine blessing, increase, and abundance; the spiritual quality of growth and prosperity
key_terms.الْخِلَافَة: Khilafa — here meaning 'succession' or 'stewardship', i.e., God's care and provision for one's descendants
key_terms.وُلْد: Wuld — children, offspring; the reward accrues to the family left behind

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the rewards of giving charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that sincere, well-given charity has two profound spiritual effects: it ensures divine protection and provision for one's descendants, and it brings the twin blessings of debt relief and lasting abundance. This teaching comes through al-Sakuni, a narrator who transmitted many practical rulings and ethical teachings from the Imam, reflecting the Shia tradition's emphasis on charitable giving as a divinely reciprocated act that transcends the individual's lifetime.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A servant does not give good charity in the world except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> betters the succession upon his children from after him’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Good charity pays off the debts, and leaves behind the Blessings’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whenever a man gives charity of the best quality, Allah replaces it for him with children in the same way (of best quality children) after his passing away.”
The Imam has also said, ‘Giving charity of best quality pays off debts and leaves behind blessings.’”
